# 3-Day Diabetes-Friendly Breakfast Plan

A nut-free, one-adult breakfast plan built to stay **under 35 g carbs** and deliver **at least 20 g protein** per meal. Portions are set to be practical and easy to prep.

## Breakfast Options by Day

### Day 1: Greek Yogurt Berry Oat Bowl
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Portion:** 1 cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt, 1/3 cup rolled oats, 1/2 cup berries, 1 tablespoon chia-free seed topping omitted due to nut allergy
- **Estimated carbs:** **31 g**
- **Estimated protein:** **24 g**
- **Estimated fiber:** **5 g**
- **Why it works:** High protein from yogurt, moderate carbs from oats and berries, and enough fiber to help blunt the glucose rise.

### Day 2: Veggie Egg Toast Plate
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/egg-fried.svg
- **Portion:** 2 large eggs, 2 egg whites, 1 slice whole-grain bread, 1 cup sautéed spinach or peppers
- **Estimated carbs:** **21 g**
- **Estimated protein:** **25 g**
- **Estimated fiber:** **5 g**
- **Why it works:** Eggs provide strong protein with very low carbs; whole-grain toast adds controlled carbs and fiber.

### Day 3: Tofu Breakfast Scramble with Toast
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- **Portion:** 7 oz firm tofu, 1 slice whole-grain bread, 1/2 cup berries
- **Estimated carbs:** **24 g**
- **Estimated protein:** **22 g**
- **Estimated fiber:** **6 g**
- **Why it works:** Tofu gives a solid protein base, while berries and whole-grain bread keep carbs moderate and fiber higher.

## Carb and Protein Check

| Day | Breakfast | Carbs | Protein | Fiber |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Greek yogurt berry oat bowl | 31 g | 24 g | 5 g |
| 2 | Veggie egg toast plate | 21 g | 25 g | 5 g |
| 3 | Tofu scramble with toast | 24 g | 22 g | 6 g |

## Quick Actions

- Action: [Button: Build a grocery list] https://www.diabetesfoodhub.org/
- Action: [Button: Save meal ideas] https://www.eatright.org/food/planning-and-prep

## Notes for Blood Sugar Stability

- Choose **plain, unsweetened** yogurt only.
- Keep berries to the listed portion; larger servings can push carbs up fast.
- Use whole-grain bread with at least **3 g fiber per slice** if possible.
- If you want more volume without many carbs, add non-starchy vegetables like spinach, mushrooms, or tomatoes.
- Because you have a **tree nut allergy**, avoid nut butters, almond toppings, and granola unless clearly nut-free.

## Sources

- American Diabetes Association meal planning: https://diabetes.org/food-nutrition
- USDA FoodData Central: https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/
- Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics: https://www.eatright.org/food/nutrition/dietary-guidelines-and-myplate
